explanation: Warren Hastings became the first Governor General of Bengal in 1774 under the Regulating Act.
The Regulating Act, 1773 first created the office of Governor-General of Bengal; none of the listed options match the Charter Act of 1833, which actually renamed the post 'Governor-General of India'.
Before Parliament began regulating the Company from 1773 onward, the Company's powers derived from Royal Charters granted by the Crown.
Florence Nightingale Award recipients carry the honorific 'Sister' as nursing staff; unable to fully verify the exact 2020 Mizoram awardee names.
Article 17 (abolition of untouchability) falls under the Right to Equality (Articles 14-18).
Sovereignty and political power in India ultimately reside in the People.
The Uniform Civil Code is mentioned in Article 44 under the Directive Principles of State Policy.
Protection of minorities' language, script, and culture is a Fundamental Right (Article 29), not a Directive Principle.
The 'rule of lapse' means unspent appropriations voted by the legislature expire at the end of the financial year.
The CAG's audit function, including of state governments, is a Union subject.
Indian judicial review rests on 'procedure established by law' rather than the American 'due process of law'.
The Collegium System governs the appointment and transfer of judges -- it belongs to the Judiciary.
Caste-based reservations are conventionally termed 'Positive Discrimination' in Indian constitutional discourse.
Liberty, equality and fraternity in the Preamble are drawn from the French Revolution's ideals.
B.P. Mandal chaired the Mandal Commission (Second Backward Classes Commission).
Mahatma Gandhi gave the Congress a formal constitution at the 1920 Nagpur session, converting it into a mass, cadre-based party.
Raja Ram Mohan Roy is chiefly remembered for opposing Sati; the movement to abolish child marriage is more closely associated with later reformers.
Gram Panchayat functions are listed in the 11th Schedule, not the 12th Schedule (which covers Municipalities).
Under Article 213, the Governor may issue an Ordinance when the state legislature is not in session and immediate action is needed.

Ambedkar gave evidence to the all-European Simon Commission (1927-28) on constitutional reforms.
Since the 7th Constitutional Amendment (1956), one person can be appointed Governor of more than one state.
The Indian federal system, with its strong centre, is most influenced by the Canadian model of federalism.
Under Article 110(3), the Speaker of the Lok Sabha certifies a bill as a money bill.
Tilak framed Swaraj not merely as a political right but as a matter of Dharma.
The 44th Amendment (1978) removed the Right to Property as a Fundamental Right, making it only a legal right under Article 300A.
Both the Supreme Court (Article 32) and High Courts (Article 226) can issue writs to enforce Fundamental Rights.
Lok Sabha's sessions are Budget, Monsoon, and Winter -- there is no formal 'Summer Session'.
Judicial review is the Supreme Court's authority to examine whether legislative or executive actions conform to the Constitution.
Both Indian and American federalism feature a federal Supreme Court empowered to interpret the Constitution.
'Universal adult franchise' is not a term used in the Preamble, though it is provided for elsewhere in the Constitution.

The National Integration Council was first constituted in 1961.
A government-directed reduction in a fixed exchange rate is termed devaluation.
The services sector is currently the largest contributor to India's national income.

The National Food Security Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha in 2013.
The Balance of Payments comprises the Current Account and the Capital Account.

The Green Revolution was most successful for wheat and rice.
The Planning Commission of India was constituted in 1950.
Mustard is a Rabi (winter) crop, not a Kharif crop.
India's land reforms included abolition of intermediaries, tenancy reforms, and reorganization of agriculture -- all of the above.
The USA has been India's top export destination in recent years.
The Yellow Revolution refers to the boost in oilseeds production.
The total value of final goods and services produced by a country's nationals is the Gross National Product (GNP).

Marginal farmers are defined as those holding land up to 1 hectare.
The Agricultural Prices Commission and Food Corporation of India were both constituted around 1965.
Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya Yojana targets rural needs like primary education, health care, drinking water, housing, and rural roads.

Jelep La pass is situated in Sikkim.

Sir Gilbert Walker discovered the Southern Oscillation phenomenon.

Census of India classifies towns of 20,000-49,999 population as Class III towns.
Industrial hazards are human-induced hazards, not natural ones.

Gujarat has the longest coastline among Indian states.
India is only a dialogue partner, not a member state, of ASEAN.
Centre-State relations are dealt with in Part XI of the Constitution.

Haryana recorded the lowest sex ratio among Indian states in the 2011 census.

M.N. Roy authored 'India in Transition' (1922).

Dadabhai Naoroji is associated with the Drain of Wealth theory.
Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in 1905.
